overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the September 14 meeting notice was timely and complete, the chair may limit public comment, and the false-data allegation was declined as outside the OML.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly changed its September 14 meeting time from 5 P.M. to 3 P.M. without notifying the complainant.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Commission posted notice of the September 14 meeting at least 48 hours prior to that meeting and included the date, time and place of the meeting, as well as the topics reasonably anticipated by the chair, we find the Board complied with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law and find no violation.

allegations.summary: Commission allegedly limited the complainant to three minutes of public input on August 24 and barred public speaking on September 14.
allegations.key_passage: Because it is within the Chair’s discretion to decide who may speak at a meeting and for how long, he did not violate the Open Meeting Law by limiting the complainant to three minutes or restricting the complainant from speaking during either the August 24 or September 14 meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Commission voted to eliminate in-person early voting using false data; the AG declined to review this non-OML matter.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government’s review concerns compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
